news_drafts.headline: North Essex Parking Partnership forecasts £223k surplus for year ending March 2027, £174k ahead of £49k budget
news_drafts.lead: The North Essex Parking Partnership, run jointly by Colchester and other councils, is on track to deliver a £223,000 surplus for the year ending March 2027, exceeding its budgeted surplus of £49,000 by £174,000. The outperformance is driven largely by penalty charge notice income running £100,000 ahead of forecast, reflecting strong enforcement performance through August. Additional unbudgeted income of £72,000 from traffic regulation order work for other authorities and Essex County Council has also contributed. The partnership's reserve is forecast to grow to £615,000 by March, £174,000 above plan. However, the council has budgeted for only a 2.5 per cent salary increase while the national pay award for local government has moved to 3.3 per cent; if Colchester negotiates a higher local rate, it would create additional financial pressure. The council has also noted uncertainty over the operational timelines of its fee structure, set through March 2030, following the halt to Essex Local Government Reorganisation.

findings.paper_title: Year End Review of Risk Management 25-26, report to Cabinet, 2 September 2026
findings.headline: 2026/27 balanced budget approved but in-year savings delivery presents medium risk to achieving balanced position
findings.detail: MTFF 2026-2031 approved by Full Council in February 2026 with balanced General Fund for 2026/27, but savings programme delivery is at risk. Failure to deliver savings or manage in-year costs could require budget adjustments, service impact or unplanned reserve use. £1m general risk contingency in place. S151 to review reserves position six-monthly and impose additional savings if required. Residual 3/3 = 9 (Medium). Future year deficits identified for 2027/28 onwards not yet addressed.
findings.matters: Legal duty to maintain balanced budget requires successful delivery of savings plan; future year deficits indicate structural financial challenges ahead of LGR.
findings.figures: Risk B: initial 3/4 = 12 (High), residual 3/3 = 9 (Medium). £1m contingency. MTFF extends to 2030/31.
findings.quote: The updated Medium-Term Financial Forecast (MTFF) 2026/27 to 203031 approved by Full Council in February 2026 contained a balanced General Fund budget for 2026/27. Failure to deliver the current year's balanced budget either through non-delivery of the savings programme or manage in year costs could result in: Inability to deliver the budget strategy as approved by Full Council

findings.paper_title: Year End Review of Risk Management 25-26, report to Cabinet, 2 September 2026
findings.headline: Fit for the Future portfolio support resource at maximum risk level (25) due to overlapping programme timelines creating shared service conflicts
findings.detail: Multiple transformation programmes place simultaneous demands on enabling services: Procurement, HR, Digital, Finance, Communications, Marketing. Risk of delays, legislative breaches, increased costs, quality issues and employee wellbeing impacts across supporting services. Initial 4/5/5 = 25 (Exceeds appetite), residual 4/4 = 16 (still Exceeds). Resource forecast, prioritization process and automation being developed.
findings.matters: Multiple critical council programmes could be delayed by capacity constraints in shared support functions, affecting delivery of savings and transformation outcomes.
findings.quote: There is a risk that overlapping timelines of multiple programmes and projects will lead to resource conflicts and delays, particularly due to their shared reliance on enabling services such as Procurement, HR, Digital, Finance, Communications, and Marketing.

findings.paper_title: Year End Review of Risk Management 25-26, report to Cabinet, 2 September 2026
findings.headline: Cyber and data security rated as highest strategic risk (score 25 initially, remains 16 after extensive controls), exceeds appetite
findings.detail: Multiple root causes: insufficient technical controls, poor staff awareness, third-party and supply chain risk. Despite substantial mitigations (CSIG board, mandatory training, Microsoft Defender, SIEM platform, off-site backup), residual risk remains very high at 4/4 = 16 and exceeds appetite for technological/data protection risks. PSN compliance work ongoing.
findings.matters: Data breach or cyber incident could result in loss of system access, service interruption, fines, and reputational damage. Remains the council's single highest-rated initial risk.
findings.figures: Risk D: initial 5/5 = 25 (Very High), residual 4/4 = 16 (Very High, Exceeds appetite)
findings.quote: Every organisation, and government organisations in particular, carries multiple risks in relation to protecting data, especially cyber threats.

findings.paper_title: Year End Review of Risk Management 25-26, report to Cabinet, 2 September 2026
findings.headline: ICT infrastructure historic systems with limited support create very high risk (15-point score) even after mitigations in place
findings.detail: Increasing reliance on IT for service delivery creates vulnerability to system failure. Multiple legacy systems have limited vendor support. Risk of severe disruption, financial impact, reputational damage and inability to meet customer requirements. Initial 3/5 = 15 (Very High), residual 3/4 = 12 (High). Risk exceeds technological risk appetite. Digital strategy and resilience reviews underway but vulnerability persists.
findings.matters: Underlying technology vulnerability poses ongoing threat to service continuity despite the council's transformation plans.
findings.figures: Risk I: initial 3/5 = 15 (Very High), residual 3/4 = 12 (High), rated as Exceeds appetite
findings.quote: The increasing reliance on IT to continue normal business leaves the Council potentially vulnerable to any major system failure, across all service areas. This vulnerability is increased due to the fact that several key systems have limited support as they are historic versions.

findings.paper_title: Year End Review of Risk Management 25-26, report to Cabinet, 2 September 2026
findings.headline: Recycling contract gate fee £111 per tonne against £45 budgeted—two-fold cost pressure in current year
findings.detail: Dry mixed recycling net gate fee significantly exceeds budget creating material cost pressure for 2025/26. Contract break point 31 July 2026 allows new tender to be let. New contract structure using 2+1+1 year breaks timed to align with kerbside rollout (1 June 2026) to mitigate overspend early in financial year. Initial 2/5/5 = 25 (Exceeds appetite), residual 5/3 = 15 (At limit).
findings.matters: Material budget overspend in waste services requires in-year mitigation and reflects inflation pressures on council operations.
findings.figures: Net gate fee £111/tonne vs budgeted £45/tonne. Initial 25 (Exceeds), residual 15 (At limit)
findings.quote: Net Gate Fee for Material Variation is £111 per tonne this is much higher than budgetted fee of £45 per tonne.

daily_post.headline: Partnership reserve building faster than planned: forecast to reach £615k by March 2027, £174k above budget
daily_post.lead: Faster reserve accumulation suggests the partnership's pricing or cost assumptions were overly conservative; significant reserves provide financial resilience but may need to be deployed or reflected in reduced charges to partner councils or users.
